1. Learned A.G.A. has informed that the notice to the informant has been served on 9.9.2024.
2. Heard Sri Rabindra Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Anit Kumar Shukla, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.
3.

Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.256 of 2024, under Sections 363, 342, 452, 506, 376(3)
I.P.C. and Section 3/4(2) POCSO Act, Police Station Pooranpur, District Pilibhit, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: The applicant and other co-accused persons are stated to have abducted the minor daughter of the informant and gang-raped her in the night of 24.05.2024 and the informant got the information about the said abduction and reached his village from Haryana, as such instituted the FIR on 21.06.2024.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
5. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case.
6. The FIR is delayed by about 28 days and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
7.

The instant case is a clear-cut matter of false implication as the applicant had filed an application against the informant to several authorities regarding cutting and felling off tree belonging to him.
The said applications have been annexed as Annexure No.11 to the affidavit accompanying the bail application.
8. There is no injury observed by the doctor conducting the medical examination of the victim.

9. The falsity of the prosecution story stands established from the statement of one witness Ramesh s/o Ram Khelawan, who has categorically stated that one of the accused person Ajeet is suffering from Cancer and is bed ridden, as such the complete prosecution story of gang-rape stands falsified.
It has also been established that the said FIR has been instituted out of vengeance.

10. The statement of the victim recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. categorically indicates that the victim was abducted in the night of 24.05.2024 and retrieved on 25.05.2024 i.e. the very next day and on being asked by the Magistrate concerned, she has categorically stated that at her house her sister, brother and grand-mother were present at the time she was abducted, as such the prosecution story stands falsified.
11.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.

12. There is criminal history of one case assigned to the applicant i.e. Case Crime No.678 of 2020,
under Sections 147, 352, 427 and 506 I.P.C., which is bailable.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 09.07.2024 and is ready to cooperate with trial.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE/INFORMANT:
13.
The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed.

CONCLUSION:

sentences.text: ?The Supreme Court in Prabhakar Tewari vs. State of U.P. And Another, 2020 (11) SCC 648 has observed that pendency of several criminal cases against an accused itself cannot be a basis for refusal of bail, if otherwise his case for bail is made out.

entities.text: Prabhakar Tewari vs. State of U.P. And Another, 2020 (11) SCC 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 15. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

16. ?A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
17.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: ?Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia vs. Directorate of Enforcement, 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
18.
?Learned A.G.A. could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
19. ?It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned A.G.A.
20.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

21. Let the applicant-Rajeev involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.

Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

23. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
